content.text: The text condemns capitalism through the exploited painters and builders of Mugsborough, who face unemployment, poverty, unsafe conditions, rushed and fraudulent work, and constant fear of dismissal. Rushton and Hunter profit through wage-cutting, surveillance, theft, and intimidation, while workers are encouraged to compete against one another. Their summer Beano takes them by brakes from Mugsborough and Windley to the Queen Elizabeth at Tubberton, where the workers eat, drink, sing, and quarrel. Socialist meetings at Windley provoke violent opposition. At the Refuge, Philpot chairs Barrington’s lecture explaining Socialism, public ownership, shorter hours, abundance, education, and equal access to life’s benefits. The workers debate and pass a resolution supporting Socialism. The next day, Philpot, Harlow, Barrington, Sawkins, and others transport the “Sixty-five” ladder to the Refuge. While raising it toward the gable, the frayed rope snaps, leaving Barrington, Bundy, and Philpot beneath the falling ladder.
